node.title: Back to the Basics, Hosted by Salesforce
node.description:
Sales Engineers of New York (SENY) and our sponsors [Iris](https://www.heyiris.ai/), [Navattic](https://www.navattic.com/) and [Minoa](https://www.minoa.io/) invite you to the final event of 2026 followed by our annual holiday party. The event will be held at [Salesforce Tower](https://maps.app.goo.gl/2j3X1owCJspfobdc7), New York, NY. The panel includes Joe Mellet from Anthropic, Anthony Westmoreland from OpenAI and Kate Stamatakos from Sierra who will be interviewed by our MC Eric Glick from Sierra.

SENY was formed in 2018 to connect all current and aspiring SEs of New York area. One of the challenges we found was that a lot of SEs (current or prospective) did not have a community where they can discuss issues related to the field of sales engineering. Join our Slack and LinkedIn channels today: [https://www.salesengineersny.com/sign-up](https://www.salesengineersny.com/sign-up)

This panel will focus on what has remained constant in today's solutions and sales process and the panelists working at top AI companies will offer their perspective on what they tell their teams to go back to all the time - "Back to the Basics".

**Logistics:** Please plan to arrive at the Salesforce Tower between 5:30 - 6 pm. The detailed instructions for checkin will be sent to the RSVPd guests. Please ***provide your full name and email*** to RSVP - pre-check-in instructions will be emailed to this address prior to the event. *If we cannot **verify you via LinkedIn**, we wont be able to add you to RSVP.*

If you have any issues, please message @senyfounders on our slack (you can join our slack at [https://www.salesengineersny.com/sign-up](https://www.salesengineersny.com/sign-up))

**Holiday-Party:** In celebration of our annual holiday party, sponsored by [Navattic](https://www.navattic.com/), [Iris](https://www.heyiris.ai/) and [Minoa](https://www.minoa.io/), guests are invited to an open bar event after the panel concludes (location close to Salesforce Tower, will be revealed on the day of event).

**Agenda**:

* 5:30 pm: Arrivals
* 6:00 PM – 6:30 PM Networking (*Check-in & Networking*)
* 6:30 PM – 6:40 PM Opening Remarks by SENY Founders / Hosts
* 6:40 PM – 7:20 PM Special Presenter, Panel Discussion & Q&A
* 7:20 PM – 7:25 PM Closing Announcements
* **[Optional]** 7:45 PM onwards **SENY Holiday Party** & Reception

Thanks and we are looking forward to seeing you!

-SENY Organizers

node.title: Rust NYC: The UnConf 2026.
node.description:
**PLEASE NOTE: YOU MUST ALSO SIGN UP HERE ON LUMA IN ORDER TO GENERATE A QR CODE TICKET, SIGNUPS THAT DO NOT DO THIS WILL NOT HAVE A TICKET.**

https://luma.com/fkm536ya

After the success of our 2025 event, we've grown almost 2000 members in 2026! So, we're doing the UnConf again. There's space for 300 of you. 20 different interactive tracks across all things Rust across an entire afternoon. A purely interactive mix of discussions, workshops, talks, demos, classes and more across all the things that you in our community have specifically requested.

We'll be covering everything from embedded Rust, to async, distributed systems, AI, GPUs, databases, and so much more!

We anticipate this will be the biggest free Rust event ever held in person, and have no intentions of slowing down.

We've gone all out this year, and hired a dedicated space at the Jay Conference Center in Chelsea for an afternoon, with 20 of the best and brightest coming together from the Rust ecosystem to present a learning opportunity quite like no other, completely for free.

If you need something to explain to your employer why this is worth your time without using PTO, we've prepped this template for you: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-UgmwFDrpk9EC2VKSVpZfannfSk_AaUHJBYpkuH_IL8/edit?usp=sharing](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-UgmwFDrpk9EC2VKSVpZfannfSk_AaUHJBYpkuH_IL8/edit?usp=sharing)

Over the coming week, we'll be announcing the talk track titles, alongside further speakers.

This event would not be possible without the community coming together to donate to the ever rising costs, and we wanted to take the opportunity to thank all of our sponsors for helping this come together:

**JetBrains have kindly funded the conference venue, and all of the other costs are being covered by Eden, Antithesis, Iroh, Empathic, Helius and Lawrence Harvey.**

With this being an afternoon event, a link to provide your employer outlining why this event is educational and worth you attending will be published here soon. We'll also have a fantastic happy hour afterwards!

***The track list is being released in blocks of 5 over the next couple of weeks, but the first 15 are here:***

**Maddie Gorman - Applied Cryptographer at Hoth**

How can Rust’s type system enforce the intricate rules of cryptography? Cryptographic schemes are made of pieces that must fit together exactly, and one misuse can break even strong cryptography. This presentation explores how real-world libraries use Rust's features to build cryptographic abstractions that enforce those rules, and the tradeoffs they make. The goal: keep the complexity inside the library, so developers get APIs that are easy to use and hard to misuse. No cryptography background needed.

**Ben Striegel - Rust Boston Organizer**

Hacking on Rust is easier than you think! This workshop will walk you through the steps of making changes to the Rust compiler itself, by futzing with the definition of pi provided by the standard library and showing you how to build projects with your customized toolchain. Whether you're a tau supremacist or think that 3 ought to be good enough for anyone, come and exercise your power over universal mathematical constants.

**Andrew Plaza - Senior Software Engineer at WebAI**

Embedded Rust has come a long way, but what does it take to actually build something useful? In this talk I will demo an embedded Rust project using Embassy and an ESP32S3. You will learn the trials and tribulations on the way to getting an espresso machine to talk and (metaphorically) roast the shot it pulled. How to share code between embedded and server components, what it takes to keep espresso metrics plus audio streams sent over the wire super-duper secure, difficulties testing and compiling Rust toolchain forks, and how to track/observe errors across a small IoT system.

**John Strassner - CTO at FutureWei Technologies**

When AI Agents Propose Knowledge: Can Rust Guard the Gate?: AI agents can now extract information and propose assertions for enterprise knowledge graphs at an unprecedented scale. However, a single plausible, incorrect assertion that passes structural checks can corrupt authoritative knowledge. We must separate probabilistic AI proposals from deterministic system authority. In this talk, I will present a neuro-symbolic governance architecture that combines symbolic verification with a strict six-state lifecycle (from Proposed to Published) before candidate knowledge can enter production. Through live Rust code, we will explore how typestate, affine ownership, and module privacy enforce legal state transitions at compile time, where rustc's guarantees end across distributed persistence boundaries, and why maintaining knowledge validity after publication remains an open challenge.

**Ethan Lowman - Database Engineer at Antithesis**

Ethan Lowman, a database engineer at Antithesis, will discuss the unique challenges involved in applying techniques such as property-based testing, fuzzing, and formal verification to stateful systems. With a special-purpose analytical tree database **built in Rust**, we'll explore, as a case study**,** how we can put our foot on the scale to find rare bugs before production.

**Saveliy Yusufov - Software Engineer at OneChronos**

High Performance Rust: Lessons From Building an FFT Library

What does it take to build a high performance numerical library in Rust? Using PhastFT as a case study, this talk examines how algorithm design, memory layout, and SIMD interact to influence performance. We’ll examine tradeoffs, challenges, and the lessons learned from implementing, benchmarking, and optimizing the library. No prior knowledge of Fourier transforms is required.

**Michael Gattozzi - Senior Software Engineer (ex-Influx Data, Ditto, Fastly)**

Understanding Async Executors

Is it a mystery to you how Async Rust is even run? Have you ever had to manually write a Future only to wonder what the heck a Context or Waker is? Also what's the deal with Send + Sync being everywhere and what even is Pin? Come learn about executors and build your own to learn what's really going on under the hood using nothing but the Standard Library!

**Jeff Schwab - Freelance Software Engineer & Founder at Unbuggy Software (ex-Bluefin)**

Crux/Leptos App Development Workshop

Join Jeff Schwab for an overview of all things Crux/Leptos app development, with an opportunity to get hands on with your own laptops to build something yourself from a provided app skeleton. You don't need Crux/Leptos experience to begin, but can join and make the most of everything to learn all you need to know to get building!

**Connor Peticca - Senior Software Engineer at Helius**

Rust & Async Io

Join Connor Petracca to discover how Helius uses Rust and Async Io to power trading infrastructure, large scale global data transfer, and petabyte scale data stores and learn how you can apply these things yourself to your workplace.

**Ryan Butler - Freelance Software Engineer (ex-World, Teleportal)**

T(rust)zone - Securing Embedded ARM Linux with Rust

Learn how to write Rust code for ARM TrustZone! We will learn what a Trusted Execution Environment is, *why* many embedded devices ship a secure OS called OP-TEE alongside Linux, and learn how to write bare-metal Rust code to communicate between the secure world and Linux.

**Devon Tietjen - Founder and CEO of Eden & RustConf 2026 speaker:**

Realtime CVE Remediation:

Cybersecurity vulnerabilities have always been risks faced by production software, but as we enter the age of the unabashed AI hacker, the scale of weaponization these tools pose is unprecedented. Agentic hackers can now exploit a vulnerability in hours, not days, and a single bad actor can attack systems at a scale only state sponsors could previously achieve. We must evolve the methodology and speed with which we protect, remediate, deploy, and observe our systems. At Eden we've been building solutions for this critical moment, and I will be discussing our approaches to solve issues for customers at every step of the software supply chain to overcome cyber threats.

**Alex Kesling - CTO & Co-Founder at Empathic**

Turtles All The Way Down

Rust lets you do amazing things. In this talk you'll learn how Doom could run at 35fps on Hubris (the Oxide Computer Company microcontroller OS) on a simulated ARM chip on WebAssembly in a web browser. Why would someone do such a thing? How does Rust empower this? Come play Doom and find out! (And learn a little about WebAssembly, embedded software, and Hubris, of two kinds, all in one talk!)

**Nick Gerace - Member of Technical Staff at East River Source Control**

The Art of Duel Wielding Against Duel Writes

A user gets a notification in their browser that it's time to take action. Messaging brokers, web socket events, browser stores, tokio tasks, channels... it all becomes too much! This talk will take participants on the speaker's (Nick Gerace) journey from contending with the "dual write problem" in his career to eventually solving it at East River Source Control (ERSC) via the Change Data Capture pattern. Your PostgreSQL WAL is already there! Dual wield it with a robust, custom Rust-powered messaging architecture to fend off your day two woes and foes.

**Greg Travis - Senior Software Engineer at Temporal Technologies**

Durably Embedded Rust Development

Come along and join Greg Travis, Senior Software Engineer on the Language Runtime SDK at Temporal Technologies to learn how to tame the famously hostile environment of embedded development with external durability.

**Yuri Astrakhan - MapLibre and OxiBUS Founder & Principal Software Engineer at Rivian**

Rust in Maps: From Bits to Pixels, at Rust Speed

Yuri Astrakhan is one of the best known engineers in the Rust geospatial community, and has led some of the biggest mapping open source projects to date. Join Yuri to find out how you can use Rust within your mapping projects to create lightning speed work, from bits to pixels.

node.title: Epictetus on dealing with difficult circumstances
node.description:
We continue our series featuring an in-depth look at the Discourses of Epictetus, a book that has literally changed my life and that I think is one of the most important of the entire Western philosophical canon, if not of philosophy worldwide.

I recommend the [Robin Waterfield translation of Epictetus](https://bookshop.org/a/80309/9780226769509), published in 2024 by the University of Chicago Press. However, a free version, based on the W.A. Oldfather translation from 1925, is available at [Wikisource](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Epictetus,_the_Discourses_as_reported_by_Arrian,_the_Manual,_and_Fragments).

<<>>

This time we will discuss Discourses 1.24, "How to combat difficult circumstances," where Epictetus argues that our worth is revealed by how we handle difficulties. Time permitting, we will then go on to talk about Discourses 1.25, which happens to be on the same topic.

<<>>

Please note that the **zoom link** will be shared with registered attendees on this page on the morning of the event, so make sure to check it before attempting to log in. Also, for security reasons (i.e., reducing the chances of "zoom bombings"), please **do not share the link** outside our group! Thanks!

node.title: Is It Love or Codependency?
node.description:
Love and codependency can look surprisingly similar from the outside.

Both can involve caring deeply, making sacrifices, supporting someone through hard times, and wanting to feel close. The difference is what is driving those behaviors and what happens to you inside the relationship.

In this session, we’ll explore the difference between healthy connection and losing yourself in another person. We’ll talk about neediness, reassurance-seeking, rescuing, overfunctioning, fear of abandonment, and feeling responsible for another person’s emotions or choices.

We’ll also look at questions many of us struggle with:

* When does supporting someone become rescuing?
* What is the difference between compromise and self-abandonment?
* Are my needs reasonable, or am I depending on one person to meet all of them?
* Am I choosing this relationship, or am I terrified of losing it?
* Can two people depend on each other without becoming codependent?

Having needs does not make someone needy. Healthy relationships involve vulnerability, support, and interdependence. The problem begins when love becomes tied to managing someone, earning your place, preventing their disappointment, or needing the relationship to feel okay about yourself.

You’ll leave with a clearer understanding of what healthy dependence looks like and how to stay connected without disappearing inside the relationship.

node.title: The Awesomely Awkward Social Club: Connect, Chat & Be You
node.description:
**Welcome to The Awesomely Awkward Social Club—because connection doesn’t have to be perfect to be real.**

🌟 **This Month's Vibe: The People We Lean On**

In this session of The Awesomely Awkward Social Club, we’re talking about the people we lean on, the people who lean on us, and what it actually means to show up for someone.

We all need support, but asking for it can feel surprisingly difficult. Some of us try to handle everything alone. Some drop hints and hope someone notices. Others become the reliable person everyone calls, then quietly wonder who would do the same for them.

Tonight, we’ll share stories about the people who helped us through difficult times, the support that genuinely made a difference, and the help that was well-intentioned but not remotely helpful.

Here’s what to expect:

* Conversation starters about the people you can count on
* Breakout rooms to share stories about giving, receiving, and asking for help
* Honest conversations about independence, reliability, and feeling needed
* Stories about unexpected support and the people who surprised us
* A chance to explore what makes someone feel safe enough to lean on

You can talk about the person who carried you through your worst year or the friend who would pick you up from the airport at 4:30 in the morning while making it very clear how they feel about your flight choices.

Come ready to listen, connect, and talk about the people who make life a little easier to carry. 💛
